author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: January CPI at 7.5% (fastest since 1982) pushed the 10Y through 2% to 2.03% and drove a bear flattening led by the 2Y (1.61%, +69 bps over twenty observations), so the day's repricing is a discount-rate and liquidity shock rather than a growth scare: favour cash-generative financials, energy and pricing-power names, underweight long-duration growth, REITs and utilities, while China eases, Poland's NBP turns hawkish with a strong zloty, and the Russia-Belarus drills keep energy and defence premia as the main pending risk.
sources_policy: Only the 2022-02-11 frozen feed (tools/digest.py, own-date --grep/--topic) and the 2022-02-11 card (tools/showcard.py, cards/2022-02-11.json) were used; no other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note, no specs/, retail_drafts/, notes/retail_* or audit/independent_* files, and no web access. The own-date exclusions file is empty. Every cited ID was re-resolved against feeds/2022-02-11.json.gz (273 distinct IDs, none used more than twice) and every quoted market value was re-checked programmatically against cards/2022-02-11.json (all sessions 2022-02-10). Numbers appear only with a card field or a headline cited in the same part; source tags follow the contract, with crypto on the prior completed daily close 2022-02-10. No numeric spot-FX is quoted; currency direction comes from dated reporting (zloty, ECB/dollar) and DXY. Previews are used only as previews (Pekao's 50 bp forecast, the March FOMC debate, Truth-Social-style launches not used). verify.py --nonretail: PASS, 8,841 body words, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0686 CNBC 'Dow slides 500 points as yields spike following red-hot inflation report' is stamped 2022-02-09 but describes the 10 February CPI reaction (misdated outcome); the reaction is taken from the card instead.

n0246 Reuters 'China government bond yields rise on faster Jan credit growth': the PBOC January credit data came late on 10 February local time and the bond-yield reaction may belong to the Asian 11 February session after the cutoff despite the day-granular stamp; omitted, and no January credit-growth claim is made.

n1466 France 24 'Biden tells US citizens to leave Ukraine...' and n1493 Guardian ''Things could go crazy quickly,' Biden warns ... as talks in Berlin fail': US-evening interview and late-ending Berlin talks could have been published after 00:00 UTC; omitted (after-cutoff risk).
n1579 Guardian 'Russia and Ukraine crisis moving wrong way, says UK defence secretary': timing of the remark is uncertain relative to the cutoff; omitted.

n0880 Seattle Times and n0881 GeekWire on Zillow shares surging / up 16%: after-hours move following after-close results, possibly measured after the cutoff; omitted (only the WSJ loss figure n0882 is used).
n0879 CNBC Kurnos on Zillow profitability: post-results interview could have aired after the cutoff; removed during self-check and replaced.
n0788 UPI 'Astra Space stock plunges after rocket failure': late-session launch and after-hours trading; omitted (after-cutoff risk, not needed).
n0826 and n1326 Reuters LIVE MARKETS pages: live blogs; not used per contract.
n0501 Verdict 'SoftBank looks to sell Alibaba shares' versus n0695 FOREX.com 'Alibaba rallies on Softbank announcement': contradictory direction; both omitted.

n1759 and n1785 Bankier.pl carry a numeric EUR/PLN quote; cited only for direction (zloty strongest in eight months, Glapinski strengthened it), with no numeric spot-FX. n1644 (Czech koruna, numeric FX) not used.

n1133 Yahoo Finance 'Apple To Enable Crypto Payments With Tap To Pay': promotional and unsupported by Apple's own headline (n1092); omitted. Other promotional/listicle items (Motley Fool hypergrowth and Shiba Inu pieces, Fundstrat targets n0897, Securities.io AVAX n0893) not used.
n0175 Geopolitical Futures 'Zero COVID and Manufacturing in China': headline does not establish a directional claim; dropped during self-check.

Pending same-day events with no own-date preview headline (UK Q4 GDP, UMich preliminary sentiment, Bank of Russia decision) and the BoJ fixed-rate offer (no own-date headline) are not mentioned; the Tokyo holiday is not stated because no own-date headline or card field states it.

Affirm and Cloudflare results have no own-date headline: Affirm's -21.42% card move is reported without a cause, Cloudflare is not discussed, and Datadog's +12.28% card move is cited only as dispersion. Twitter (not on the card) is discussed via headline only, with no price.

n1625 StockWatch.pl Pekao forecast of a 50 bp hike is a preview; the size of the 8 February MPC decision is not stated because the decision headline (n1723) only says rates are the highest in almost nine years.
n1762 PolsatNews.pl quote 'I will urge tightening of monetary policy' is quoted literally without attributing the speaker beyond the headline.
FTX's Super Bowl bitcoin giveaway (n0918) is cited as an announced plan only; the game and the ads airing come after the cutoff.
